text:
This looks like early 2023. The fed funds rate is at 4.83%, which matches February or March 2023 (it was 4.57% in January and 4.65% in February). The 2-year yield at 4.10% and 10-year at 3.55% suggest a month-end when yields had fallen, so January 2023 (10-year at 3.51%, 2-year at 4.20%) fits, or possibly March 2023.

Checking against the CPI and rate figures:
- Headline CPI at 5.99% YoY is consistent with February 2023, when it was 6.0%. Core CPI at 5.53% fits as well, since February 2023 core was 5.5%.
- The 12-month change in the policy rate is +4.5, which means the rate a year earlier was about 0.33%. Fed funds was about 0.08% in February 2022, so that does not fit. March 2022 was 0.20% and April 2022 was 0.33%. This points to April 2023 if the rate were 4.83%, but the actual April 2023 rate was 4.83%, which matches.
- However, CPI in April 2023 was 4.9%, which does not match. In March 2023 the fed funds rate was 4.65%.

The CPI figures fit the February 2023 release, but that release was published in March 2023. Yields at month-end March 2023 were a 2-year of 4.06% and a 10-year of 3.47%. The 1-month equity return of +3.3% fits March 2023 (S&P up 3.7%), and Treasury returns of +5% for the 7-10y also fit March. The 3-month change in the 2-year of -0.31 is plausible. Unemployment at 3.6% fits the February 2023 reading (3.6%), and payrolls at about 351k average fit too. Gold up 7.4% in March 2023 fits. The fed funds figure was likely an effective-rate average of 4.65% in March, and the 4.83% matches the later reading, so I will go with March 2023.
